genres.name: Goa trance
genres.description: Born at beach parties in Goa, India, where DJs in the late 80s mixed EBM, acid and industrial. Melodic, with Eastern scales, analog synths and long arrangements.

production.bass: Pulsing 16th-note bassline, often from an analog synth
production.kick: Softer kick than later styles, with lots of 909 percussion
production.atmosphere: Oriental scales, acid (TB-303) lines, long build-ups

genres.name: Old-school UK psy
genres.description: The mid-90s London scene that turned the Goa sound into tighter, crazier and more danceable psytrance. Key to the transition from Goa to modern psy.

production.atmosphere: Humour, weird samples, fewer oriental scales over time

genres.name: Psytrance
genres.description: The name that stuck in the late 90s as the sound became more digital, harder and less oriental. The umbrella term for everything that follows.

production.bass: The rolling bass starts replacing Goa lines
production.atmosphere: More FX and samples, less melody

genres.name: Full-on
genres.description: The Israeli school: rolling bass, strong leads and non-stop energy. The most widespread form of psy.

production.bass: Classic rolling bass: kick plus three bass notes in between
production.kick: Strong, punchy kick with a short tail
production.atmosphere: Big melodies, rise/fall FX, breakdowns with vocal samples

genres.name: Morning full-on
genres.description: The brighter, euphoric branch of full-on, made for festival sunrises. Melody comes first.

production.bass: Rolling bass with a softer tone
production.atmosphere: Major-key melodies, bright pads, fewer aggressive FX

genres.name: Night full-on
genres.description: Darker, more aggressive full-on with lots of FX and less melody. The bridge to dark psy.

production.atmosphere: Dark leads, dense FX, fewer melodic themes

tracks.artist: Tristan, Burn In Noise, Avalon, Altruism
tracks.title: The God Molecule

genres.name: Brazilian full-on
genres.description: Brazil became one of the biggest psy scenes; the sound is modern, clean and built for big festival moments.

production.atmosphere: Big drops, festival build-ups

genres.name: Neo-goa
genres.description: A return to the 90s sound with modern production: melodies, acid lines and Goa aesthetics.

production.atmosphere: Acid lines, oriental melodies, long arrangements

genres.name: Mainstream psy
genres.description: Psy that reached the big EDM festivals: shorter tracks, clear drops and a radio-friendly approach. Many scene fans keep their distance from it.

production.atmosphere: Vocals and ethnic samples, build-up → drop structure

tracks.artist: Armin van Buuren vs Vini Vici feat. Hilight Tribe
tracks.title: Great Spirit

genres.name: Progressive psy
genres.description: Slower, more minimal and more hypnotic. Groove and gradual development instead of constant pounding. The most popular style in clubs today.

production.bass: Off-beat bass or shorter rolling bass, heavy sidechain
production.atmosphere: Slow filter sweeps, minimal melodies, hypnotic loops

genres.name: Offbeat prog
genres.description: Melodic progressive built on the offbeat bass: the bass hits between the kicks for a bouncy, driving pulse. Big in Hamburg and across German and Danish clubs.

production.bass: Offbeat bass: one short note between every two kicks
production.atmosphere: Melodic leads and uplifting breakdowns, cleaner and brighter than dark prog

genres.name: Zenonesque
genres.description: A minimal, dry sound gathered around the Australian label Zenon Records. Glitch details and a techno pulse.

production.atmosphere: Glitches and micro-samples, lots of space in the mix

genres.name: Psy-techno
genres.description: Progressive psy meets techno: straight kick, dark atmosphere, psychedelic FX instead of a rolling bass.

production.bass: Techno bass, rumble under the kick
production.atmosphere: Dark pads, psychedelic FX and acid details

genres.name: Twilight
genres.description: Between full-on and dark: a dark atmosphere, but with groove and melodies.

production.atmosphere: Dark melodies, mysterious mood

genres.name: Dark psy
genres.description: The Russian and German scenes: horror samples, distortion, an abstract sound without classic melodies.

production.atmosphere: Horror samples, metallic sounds, abstract structure

genres.name: Suomisaundi
genres.description: Finnish free-form psy: humour, weird samples, chaotic structure. Breaks the rules on purpose.

production.atmosphere: Humour, live playing, strange transitions

genres.name: Forest
genres.description: Organic forest sounds and a dark but natural atmosphere. A frequent point of debate with dark psy.

production.atmosphere: Forest sounds, rustling, insects, mystical mood

genres.name: Hi-tech
genres.description: Extremely fast, precisely programmed, packed with micro-sounds.

production.atmosphere: Thousands of micro-samples, rapid changes, sci-fi FX

genres.name: Psycore
genres.description: The fastest and heaviest end of the spectrum, with industrial and noise influences.

production.atmosphere: Noise, distortion, chaotic transitions

genres.name: Psybient / Psychill
genres.description: Ambient and downtempo for festival chill-out zones. Psychedelic sounds without a dance beat.

production.bass: Deep, slow pads instead of a bassline
production.kick: Soft kick or none at all
production.atmosphere: Vast reverb, ethnic instruments, layered textures

festivals: Chill-out stages at Boom and Ozora

genres.name: Psy-world
genres.description: Psychedelia with ethnic instruments and rhythms from around the world: sitar, didgeridoo, tabla, vocals.

production.kick: Ethnic percussion instead of a clean kick
production.atmosphere: Ethnic instruments and vocals

genres.name: Psy-dub
genres.description: Dub bass and reverb combined with psychedelic production techniques.

production.atmosphere: Delay and reverb effects, reggae/dub rhythms

genres.name: Psystep
genres.description: Psychedelic sounds over half-time dubstep rhythms.

production.atmosphere: Psychedelic FX, ethnic details

genres.name: Psy-glitch / Psybass
genres.description: Glitch, bass music and psychedelia: extremely detailed production and heavy bass.

production.atmosphere: Micro-edits, glitches, spatial FX

genres.name: Nitzhonot
genres.description: An Israeli offshoot of Goa from the late 90s (Hebrew for “victories”). Hard kick, anthemic Eastern melodies and long uplifting sections. It went mainstream in Israel and in the early 2000s melted into full-on and “uplifting” psy.

production.kick: Hard, loud kick, faster than Goa
production.atmosphere: Anthemic leads, Eastern scales, long build-ups without much darkness

genres.name: South African scene
genres.description: Since the early 2000s Cape Town has been one of the strongest psy scenes outside Europe and Israel. The sound ranges from melodic progressive (Protoculture) to energetic full-on, and open-air festivals are part of local culture.

production.bass: Rolling bass, from soft progressive to full-on weight
production.atmosphere: Melodic themes, sunny festival energy

genres.name: Swedish minimal prog
genres.description: Around 2000, Swedish producers (Vibrasphere, Atmos, Son Kite, Noma, Human Blue) stripped psytrance to the bone: less melody, more rhythm and space. Vibrasphere's album Echo (2000) is considered one of the foundations of modern progressive.

production.bass: Short, tight bass notes with heavy sidechain
production.atmosphere: Hypnotic repetition, micro filter changes, little melody

genres.name: Dark progressive
genres.description: The darker side of progressive, halfway between the Zenon sound and darkpsy. Slower than dark psy, but with the same unease and plenty of psychedelic detail.

production.atmosphere: Dark pads, glitch and horror FX, lots of space

tracks.artist: Freedom Fighters x Pspiralife x HypoGeo
tracks.title: Subconscious

genres.name: Psybreaks
genres.description: The psytrance sound over breakbeat rhythms. Born in the UK in the early 2000s (Digitalis, Mood Deluxe, Slack Baba), later pushed by Hedflux, Bad Tango and Monk3y Logic, with Broken Robot as a key label.

production.bass: Psy rolling or acid bass over a broken beat
production.atmosphere: Psy FX and acid lines with a funk/breaks groove

tracks.title: Zen and the Art of Psy Breaks

genres.name: Psychedelic rock
genres.description: The 60s and 70s psychedelic movement gave psytrance its name, its ethos and its first travellers: Goa became a hippie destination in the late 60s, long before anyone played electronic music there. Gong's Steve Hillage later founded System 7, a direct bridge into the dance scene.

production.bass: Live bass guitar, often hypnotic and repetitive
production.atmosphere: Long improvised jams, tape echo, spacey organs and early synths

genres.name: EBM / Industrial
genres.description: Electronic Body Music: hard sequenced bass, shouted vocals and a militant pulse. One of the main ingredients early Goa DJs mixed, and the source of the driving sequenced basslines.

production.bass: Sequenced, gated synth bass on 8th or 16th notes
production.atmosphere: Cold, aggressive, metallic samples

genres.name: New beat
genres.description: A short-lived Belgian scene that slowed EBM down and added acid lines and samples. Part of the record bags in Goa in the late 80s.

production.atmosphere: Dark samples, acid lines, a hypnotic slow pulse

genres.name: Acid house
genres.description: Chicago house built around the squelching Roland TB-303. The acid line became one of the defining sounds of Goa and is still all over psytrance.

production.bass: TB-303 acid line with resonance and accent tweaks
production.atmosphere: Raw, minimal, the 303 in the spotlight

genres.name: Detroit techno
genres.description: Futuristic machine music from Detroit, made by Juan Atkins (Model 500), Derrick May (Rhythim Is Rhythim) and Kevin Saunderson (Inner City). It defined the straight 4/4 grid, the sci-fi mood and the producer-as-programmer idea that trance and psy built on.

production.bass: Synth bass locked to the kick
production.atmosphere: Futuristic strings and pads, sci-fi melancholy

genres.name: Frankfurt trance
genres.description: German trance developing in parallel with Goa, around Sven Väth and labels like Harthouse and Eye Q. More a cousin of psy than a parent, the two scenes shared ideas, DJs and dancefloors.

production.atmosphere: Long builds, arpeggios, euphoric pads
